newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australia bonds pause, up channel intact.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australia bonds pause, up channel intact.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract's rally of the past few days stalled in SYCOM trading, but the rising channel which started at the beginning of the month remained intact.
*The 10-year contract held support at around 92.120 after 92.180 again proved a firm barrier on the upside.
The Australian 10-year bond futures contract's heady rally of the past few days stalled in SYCOM trading, but the rising channel which started at the beginning of the remained intact.
A sharp fall in U.S. Treasuries at one stage on Wednesday after further data suggested that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy next month took some heat out of the local market, analysts said.
The June 10-year bond contract ended SYCOM at 92.150 compared with Wednesday's 92.160 pit close, but held support at around 92.120 after 92.180 again proved a firm barrier.
A break of 92.180 is expected to find further resistance at 92.210 and again at around 92.230/92.240.
The latter area represents the topside of the current rising channel and is also a 50 percent retracement of the mid-February to early April sell-off from 92.760 to 91.700.
On the downside, support is expected at 92.080 and then at the psychological 92.000 level, which is also the bottom line of the bullish channel.
There is no major local data due until Wednesday's March quarter CPI report unless the long awaited verdict on the "living wage" claim is finally made in the interim period.

A stronger than expected 0.9 percent rise in March industrial production and a rise to 84.1 percent in capacity utilisation sent the U.S. bond market lower on Wednesday, and overshadowed a 6.4 percent decline in housing starts for the same period.
The market pared the fall by the close, but sentiment remains bearish as the Federal Open Market Committee is expected to endorse another tightening in the Fed funds rate when it meets on May 20.
